Open the page in a browser with a screen reader active (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver). 2. Open the Heading List (VoiceOver: VO+U -> Headings; NVDA: Insert+F7 -> Headings). 3. Inspect the tree: level 1 is immediately followed by level 3 items, followed by level 2 items. expected_behavior: Document outline progresses logically (h1 -> h2 -> h3) with sibling sections sharing identical heading tiers. actual_behavior: Level 2 is skipped initially; sibling article sections oscillate between level 3 and level 2. trend: new ``` --- ### Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) #### 1. Orphaned / Content-Free Heading Element - **Location**: `BlogPost.jsx:22` (`

Getting Started

`) - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users and cognitive accessibility users. - **Why this matters**: Heading elements announce the presence of an upcoming section. When an AT user jumps directly to `

Getting Started

`, they encounter zero descriptive or interactive content before immediately colliding with `

Tools and Resources

`. This creates cognitive friction and confusion regarding whether content failed to load. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (Level AA). - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Either provide the corresponding introductory text/list content beneath `Getting Started`, or remove the heading until the content is ready. --- ### Enhancements (best practice not met) 1. **Document Landmark Scope**: - `BlogPost.jsx:3` uses `
`. When rendered within a full application layout, ensure the article is contained within a top-level `
` landmark region to allow assistive technology users to jump directly to the primary page contents. 2. **Title Consistency**: - Verify that the page `` tag matches or incorporates the `<h1>` text ("Introduction to Web Accessibility") per WCAG 2.4.2 (Page Titled). --- ### What's Missing (gaps and unhandled conditions) - **Missing Content Block**: The `Getting Started` section lacks body text, code samples, or guidance. - **Missing Landmark Context**: Standalone `<article>` without clear structural relationship to document root or main content container. - **Missing Skip Target**: If part of a full site layout, ensure the `<h1>` or `<article>` has `id="main-content"` to pair with a skip navigation link. --- ### Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |---|---|---| | Screen reader | **HIGH** | Heading levels skip levels and invert document hierarchy (h1 → h3 → h2) | | Keyboard-only | **LOW** | Static text content with no interactive controls or focus traps | | Low vision | **LOW** | Text contrast satisfies WCAG AA; clean typography and generous line height | | Cognitive | **MEDIUM** | Inconsistent information architecture and orphaned section header ("Getting Started") | | Vestibular & motion | **LOW** | Static layout with no animation or transitions | | Auditory access | **LOW** | No audio or video media present | | Environmental contrast | **LOW** | Color contrast: `#0066cc` on `#fff` is 5.68:1; `#666` on `#fff` is 5.71:1 (both > 4.5:1) | --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user**: Navigating by headings is erratic. VoiceOver / NVDA will announce `Heading Level 3, Why Accessibility Matters` immediately following `Heading Level 1`, causing the user to question if an outer category was skipped. Subsequent `Heading Level 2` announcements ("Tools and Resources") will incorrectly imply a broader scope than the introductory sections. - **Keyboard-only user**: No custom interactive components exist; standard sequential browser reading applies. - **Low vision user**: Line height (1.6) and contrast ratios meet requirements. Headings visually scale cleanly (`32px` -> `24px` -> `18px`). - **Cognitive user**: The abrupt transition from `Getting Started` to `Tools and Resources` without text creates an unexpected dead end in the reading flow. --- ### Recommended Remediation ```jsx const BlogPost = () => { return ( <article className="blog-post"> <h1>Introduction to Web Accessibility</h1> <h2>Why Accessibility Matters</h2> <p> Web accessibility ensures that everyone, including people with disabilities, can access and interact with web content effectively. </p> <h2>WCAG Guidelines</h2> <p>The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) provide a set of standards...</p> <h3>Common Issues</h3> <ul> <li>Missing alt text for images</li> <li>Poor color contrast</li> <li>Inaccessible forms</li> </ul> <h2>Getting Started</h2> <p>Begin by evaluating existing pages using automated tooling and keyboard navigation checks.</p> <h2>Tools and Resources</h2> <p>There are many tools available to help with accessibility testing...</p> <h2>Conclusion</h2> <p>Accessibility is not optional. It's a fundamental part of web development.</p> </article> ); }; export default BlogPost; ``` --- ### Verdict Justification - **Why REVISE**: While the component passes automated HTML syntax validation and maintains sufficient color contrast, the structural heading design violates WCAG 1.3.1. Correcting the heading levels from `<h3>` to `<h2>` and populating or removing the empty `Getting Started` section will bring the document outline into full conformance, enabling an upgrade to **ACCEPT**. ### Open Questions (unscored) - Is "Common Issues" intended as a subsection under "WCAG Guidelines" (as shown in the remediation above), or is it an independent top-level topic (which would warrant an `<h2>`)? - Was `Getting Started` intended to introduce "Tools and Resources", or is its body paragraph missing from the fixture?
